newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere mixed, Bank shares up in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere mixed, Bank shares up in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares were mixed on Monday on the Beirut Stock Exchange as A shares fell to a new all-time low of $10.125 from Friday's $10.25 while B shares rose to $10.75 from $10.625.
The A shares changed hands all last week on the last record low of $10.25, which they first hit on January 17.
The A shares began trading on the Beirut Secondary Market at $111 in June 1994 or $11.1 after Solidere's 10-for-one stock split which took effect earlier this year.
Demand for Solidere A shares remained high with 127,365 shares changing hands from 109,000 on Friday. This compared with a daily turnover of 40-50,000 in previous weeks and 80-100,000 last week.
Banque Audi shares continued their rally closing at $18.375 from Friday's $18.25 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $13.125 from $13.25.
Turnover in BLC was 22,000 shares from 10,000 and 13,000 Audi shares changed hands against Friday's 10,253.
Total BSE turnover was 220,286 shares for a value of $2,439,361 against 178,330 shares for a value of $1,864,123 on Thursday.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The BLOM stock index fell 0.25 percent to 891.82, the LISPI rose 0.16 percent to 82.50 and the LIBX rose 0.82 percent to 114.53.
